key_insight: This paper argues that strong performance on math benchmarks does not necessarily mean an LLM truly understands mathematical structure. The authors introduce a new way to diagnose missing mathematical primitives and use that diagnosis to improve post-training.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the gap between superficial math-solving ability and genuine structural mathematical understanding in large language models, and asks how to identify and repair that gap.
method: Define and use "Mathematical Primitive" as a diagnostic concept to probe specific structural math capabilities in LLMs.
Systematically evaluate models to separate rote problem-solving from deeper mathematical understanding.
Leverage the diagnostic findings to guide post-training improvements that strengthen mathematical reasoning.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this provides a more precise framework for evaluating math reasoning beyond final-answer accuracy. It also offers a path to make model improvements more targeted, interpretable, and effective during post-training.
visual_elements: A pipeline diagram showing diagnosis of mathematical primitives followed by repair/post-training.
A comparison chart contrasting benchmark accuracy vs. structural mathematical understanding.
An icon-based taxonomy of different mathematical primitives or reasoning skills.
Before-and-after performance plots showing improvement after targeted post-training.
paper_title: The Missing Primitive: Diagnosing and Repairing Mathematical Reasoning in Large Language Models
paper_authors: Shuo Xing, Zilin Dai, Chengyuan Qian, Fangzhou Lin, Wenjing Chen
